open: A house viewing gives you thirty minutes. The decision stays with you for years.
story: I'm Halo. My partner and I are looking for our first home. Every listing looked fine in the photos. But I kept wondering: how long is the walk home at night? Is the morning train full? What does a month really cost? I could look at a home for thirty minutes. I couldn't live in it before I signed.
problem: In Korea, about three in four victims of deposit fraud are in their twenties and thirties. The people with the least experience carry the biggest risk.
idea: So before you sign, an AI household lives thirty days in each home.
demo1: Here, a couple who both work in Pangyo say it in plain words: two salaries, two hundred million won saved, a home under seven hundred million. Muse Spark reads it and calls real tools: real purchase records, prices in won, and the door-to-door commute for each home.
demo2a: Pick two homes, and the same household lives the same month in both. Muse decides each day: when to leave, walk or ride, the park or the store, and says why. The engine counts every minute and every won.
demo3: A listing might say five minutes to the station. Living there showed more: one home is seven minutes from work, the other twenty-four. From one station they walk home after dark ten times a month, from the other, thirty-six. Ithaca never picks for you. It shows you, and you decide.
trust: Before you see the report, code re-checks every number, and a separate Muse judge rejects any sentence the record does not support.
metaa: We also built it for Meta HQ in Menlo Park: Caltrain timetables, ZIP-level rent, the same thirty days. Switch the model to Muse Spark Open, the open-weights model, and the month runs again. If it's busy, Muse Spark one point three steps in, and every reply says which model answered.
built: Muse Spark talks and decides. A Muse judge checks the report. And Muse Code wrote every line of product code, starting October twenty-eighth.
close: We're still looking for our home. This time, we'll live there first.
